newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. probe suspects 134 massacres in ex-Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. probe suspects 134 massacres in ex-Zaire.

text.p: A U.N. human rights investigator said he received information on 134 incidents of massacres of Rwanda refugees in the former eastern Zaire, most of them carried out by forces loyal to now-President Laurent Kabila, according to a report released on Friday.

The investigator, Roberto Garreton of Chile, has been denied further entry to Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo after his earlier report that cited 40 massacre sites. His new, harsher report was based on interviews with survivors in Rwanda as well as U.N. relief workers interviewed in May.

The new report, dated July 2, said 68 percent of the allegations received were traced to rebels loyal to Kabila and their allies and the remainder were committed by the former Zairean army under ousted President Mobuto Sese Seko or Rwandan Hutu militia that controlled the refugee camps.

Over a million Hutus in 1994 crossed into what was then Zaire fearing reprisals for the genocide in Rwanda of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners. The bulk returned home but U.N. relief officials say up to 200,000 remain unaccounted.

"According to the information received, several thousand people were killed, including large number of women and children," the Garreton report said, adding that tens of thousands of others disappeared into forests where many probably died of malnutrition and disease.

"The methods used," he said, were "deliebrate, premeditated massacres, the disperal of refugees to inaccessible inhospitalble areas, the systematic blockade of humanitarian assistance and the stubborn opposition thus far to any attempt to conduct an impartial objective investigation into the very serious allegations."
